raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA, a newly created agency, may cause delays and non‑compliance with World Bank procurement rules.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit experienced procurement specialists, provide bank‑led training, develop a detailed procurement manual and use bank technical assistance to review all procurement documents.",
      "evidence": "Section 66: \"Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Limited financial management experience in ADISA and MIPA could lead to fiduciary weaknesses and audit findings.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Hire qualified finance specialists, conduct on‑the‑job FM training, implement a Project Operations Manual with clear internal controls, and ensure regular bank supervision and audits.",
      "evidence": "Section 62‑64: \"...ADISA and MIPA have limited experience... capacity strengthening would be recommended...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Disbursements under the Results‑Based Financing are contingent on achieving DLIs; failure to meet DLIs could create funding shortfalls.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Establish robust monitoring of DLI progress, provide targeted technical assistance for early‑win activities, and set up contingency plans for partial DLI achievement.",
      "evidence": "Section 31‑32: \"No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Complex coordination among multiple ministries and agencies may cause implementation delays and inconsistent reforms.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Activate the Inter‑ministerial Public Services Committee and the Project Steering Committee with clear terms of reference, schedule weekly/monthly coordination meetings, and document MoUs for each agency.",
      "evidence": "Section 58‑59: \"Inter‑sectoral reforms... necessarily entail complex coordination... the Prime Minister’s office and the DU will play an important role...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Focus on state‑of‑the‑art digital services and the urban CSC may marginalise poor, rural, women and Roma populations.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Deploy assisted internet access points, maintain non‑digital service channels, and run targeted outreach campaigns for disadvantaged groups as outlined in Table 3.",
      "evidence": "Section 27‑28 and Table 3: \"risk that the focus on state‑of‑the‑art means... could diminish access of the poor and vulnerable... assisted digital access, improving existing service access points...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Construction of the new Citizen Service Center may generate dust, noise, waste and traffic impacts.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement the Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, monitor emissions and waste, and obtain all required environmental permits.",
      "evidence": "Section 70‑71: \"Potential environmental impacts... dust and noise, waste generation... mitigated through sound construction practices and implementation of a project specific EMP.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Lack of existing IT systems and interoperability among key agencies could hinder automation and e‑service delivery.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Develop a phased integration architecture, conduct thorough testing, leverage NAIS as the interoperability platform, and provide ICT advisory support to agencies.",
      "evidence": "Section 11‑12: \"Seven institutions have no IT system... need to improve inter‑operability of electronic registers... NAIS is working to connect existing online registries...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Delays in passing the omnibus legislation required for regulatory reforms could stall business‑process re‑engineering.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prepare draft legislation early, maintain continuous dialogue with the Parliament’s legislative committee, and track approval milestones in the project schedule.",
      "evidence": "Section 19‑20: \"Reform of government services and repeal of licenses... will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Operating and maintenance costs of the CSC may exceed budgeted amounts, threatening financial sustainability.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Conduct a detailed cost‑benefit analysis, explore PPP or concession models for building management, and set aside a reserve for recurring operational expenses.",
      "evidence": "Section 50‑51: \"Significant upfront financial costs... operating costs for the CSC will likely be offset... Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Front‑office staff may resist changes to service delivery processes, reducing reform effectiveness.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement a change‑management program with training, performance incentives, and clear communication of benefits to staff.",
      "evidence": "Section 58‑59: \"Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts... diagnostics of the political economy of reforms and a focus on change management can help identify and mitigate these risks.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Baseline surveys and performance data may be of poor quality, compromising DLI verification.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Use third‑party validation for surveys, pilot test instruments, and establish clear data‑collection protocols before full rollout.",
      "evidence": "Section 44‑45: \"The project supports the DU... verification protocols... where appropriate, third party validations will be deployed to verify DLI results.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Macroeconomic shocks could increase payment arrears and strain the government’s ability to meet salary‑related EEPs.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain fiscal buffers, monitor macro indicators, and adjust disbursement schedules if necessary.",
      "evidence": "Section 49: \"Inadequate commitment controls and excessive growth in payment arrears emerged as a serious problem in recent years.\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Citizen Feedback Mechanism may not be fully utilized, limiting its value for performance management.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated CFM analytics team, set minimum response‑rate targets, and integrate feedback results into quarterly performance reports.",
      "evidence": "Section 39‑42: \"A citizen feedback mechanism will be rolled out... The DU will analyze and present the data...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Changes in political leadership could reduce high‑level commitment to the reform agenda.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Secure formal legislative endorsements, embed reforms in the National Strategy for Development and Integration, and maintain continuous engagement with the Prime Minister’s office.",
      "evidence": "Section 45: \"High level political commitment and push, which is a great asset...\""
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Overall procurement risk remains high because the PMU is not yet fully staffed and lacks consolidated finance‑procurement procedures.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Accelerate recruitment of procurement and finance specialists, adopt standard World Bank procurement templates, and use bank procurement specialists for early reviews.",
      "evidence": "Section 66‑67: \"Procurement risk rating is High... PMU not yet fully set up...\""
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA, a newly created agency, may cause delays and non‑compliance with World Bank procurement rules.
risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced procurement specialists, provide bank‑led training, develop a detailed procurement manual and use bank technical assistance to review all procurement documents.
risks.evidence: Section 66: "Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency."

risks.description: Limited financial management experience in ADISA and MIPA could lead to fiduciary weaknesses and audit findings.
risks.mitigation: Hire qualified finance specialists, conduct on‑the‑job FM training, implement a Project Operations Manual with clear internal controls, and ensure regular bank supervision and audits.
risks.evidence: Section 62‑64: "...ADISA and MIPA have limited experience... capacity strengthening would be recommended..."

risks.description: Disbursements under the Results‑Based Financing are contingent on achieving DLIs; failure to meet DLIs could create funding shortfalls.
risks.mitigation: Establish robust monitoring of DLI progress, provide targeted technical assistance for early‑win activities, and set up contingency plans for partial DLI achievement.
risks.evidence: Section 31‑32: "No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved."

risks.description: Complex coordination among multiple ministries and agencies may cause implementation delays and inconsistent reforms.
risks.mitigation: Activate the Inter‑ministerial Public Services Committee and the Project Steering Committee with clear terms of reference, schedule weekly/monthly coordination meetings, and document MoUs for each agency.
risks.evidence: Section 58‑59: "Inter‑sectoral reforms... necessarily entail complex coordination... the Prime Minister’s office and the DU will play an important role..."

risks.description: Focus on state‑of‑the‑art digital services and the urban CSC may marginalise poor, rural, women and Roma populations.
risks.mitigation: Deploy assisted internet access points, maintain non‑digital service channels, and run targeted outreach campaigns for disadvantaged groups as outlined in Table 3.
risks.evidence: Section 27‑28 and Table 3: "risk that the focus on state‑of‑the‑art means... could diminish access of the poor and vulnerable... assisted digital access, improving existing service access points..."

risks.description: Construction of the new Citizen Service Center may generate dust, noise, waste and traffic impacts.
risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, monitor emissions and waste, and obtain all required environmental permits.
risks.evidence: Section 70‑71: "Potential environmental impacts... dust and noise, waste generation... mitigated through sound construction practices and implementation of a project specific EMP."

risks.description: Lack of existing IT systems and interoperability among key agencies could hinder automation and e‑service delivery.
risks.mitigation: Develop a phased integration architecture, conduct thorough testing, leverage NAIS as the interoperability platform, and provide ICT advisory support to agencies.
risks.evidence: Section 11‑12: "Seven institutions have no IT system... need to improve inter‑operability of electronic registers... NAIS is working to connect existing online registries..."

risks.description: Delays in passing the omnibus legislation required for regulatory reforms could stall business‑process re‑engineering.
risks.mitigation: Prepare draft legislation early, maintain continuous dialogue with the Parliament’s legislative committee, and track approval milestones in the project schedule.
risks.evidence: Section 19‑20: "Reform of government services and repeal of licenses... will be implemented through omnibus legislation, expected to be passed by the end of 2016."

risks.description: Operating and maintenance costs of the CSC may exceed budgeted amounts, threatening financial sustainability.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a detailed cost‑benefit analysis, explore PPP or concession models for building management, and set aside a reserve for recurring operational expenses.
risks.evidence: Section 50‑51: "Significant upfront financial costs... operating costs for the CSC will likely be offset... Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance."

risks.description: Front‑office staff may resist changes to service delivery processes, reducing reform effectiveness.
risks.mitigation: Implement a change‑management program with training, performance incentives, and clear communication of benefits to staff.
risks.evidence: Section 58‑59: "Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts... diagnostics of the political economy of reforms and a focus on change management can help identify and mitigate these risks."

risks.description: Baseline surveys and performance data may be of poor quality, compromising DLI verification.
risks.mitigation: Use third‑party validation for surveys, pilot test instruments, and establish clear data‑collection protocols before full rollout.
risks.evidence: Section 44‑45: "The project supports the DU... verification protocols... where appropriate, third party validations will be deployed to verify DLI results."

risks.description: Macroeconomic shocks could increase payment arrears and strain the government’s ability to meet salary‑related EEPs.
risks.mitigation: Maintain fiscal buffers, monitor macro indicators, and adjust disbursement schedules if necessary.
risks.evidence: Section 49: "Inadequate commitment controls and excessive growth in payment arrears emerged as a serious problem in recent years."

risks.description: Citizen Feedback Mechanism may not be fully utilized, limiting its value for performance management.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated CFM analytics team, set minimum response‑rate targets, and integrate feedback results into quarterly performance reports.
risks.evidence: Section 39‑42: "A citizen feedback mechanism will be rolled out... The DU will analyze and present the data..."

risks.description: Changes in political leadership could reduce high‑level commitment to the reform agenda.
risks.mitigation: Secure formal legislative endorsements, embed reforms in the National Strategy for Development and Integration, and maintain continuous engagement with the Prime Minister’s office.
risks.evidence: Section 45: "High level political commitment and push, which is a great asset..."

risks.description: Overall procurement risk remains high because the PMU is not yet fully staffed and lacks consolidated finance‑procurement procedures.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate recruitment of procurement and finance specialists, adopt standard World Bank procurement templates, and use bank procurement specialists for early reviews.
risks.evidence: Section 66‑67: "Procurement risk rating is High... PMU not yet fully set up..."
